name: RBC Bearings Incorporated
sector: Industrials / Aerospace & defense bearings and engineered components
moat_justification: Moderate-strong narrow moat: mission-critical, highly engineered precision bearings and components designed into aerospace/defense and industrial platforms, where requalification of a substitute supplier is slow and costly, giving sole/primary-source stickiness and proven pricing power (gross margin 37.9% FY2022 → 44.4% FY2025/26, 47.7% in Q1 FY2027). Measured ROIC proxy is only mid-to-high single digits (6.0% FY2023 → 7.8% FY2026 after 11-12% in FY2019-20) because the 2021 Dodge acquisition loaded the balance sheet with goodwill/intangibles — that caps the score at 6 despite the margin record; larger rivals (Timken, SKF, Schaeffler) contest the industrial side and OEM customers are concentrated and powerful.
fragility_flags: SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2021, 2022 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality precision-bearings franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $498.52 the weighted IRR is only 6.6% (Tier D, IV@15% $146.04); it clears the 15% hurdle only near $146, about 71% below the current price.
moat_for: Designed-in, mission-critical bearings/components — requalifying a substitute on an aerospace or defense platform is slow and costly
Proven pricing power: gross margin 37.9% (FY2022) → 44.4% (FY2025/26) and 47.7% in Q1 FY2027
Sole/primary-source positions and a $2.3B backlog (Q1 FY2027) across commercial aero, defense and space programs
Proprietary plain-bearing / engineered-component know-how built over decades; fragmented niche leadership
moat_against: Measured ROIC proxy only 6.0-7.8% FY2023-26 — Dodge (2021) goodwill/intangibles bloat the capital base and returns have not yet re-earned a wide-moat grade
Larger diversified rivals (Timken, SKF, Schaeffler) and powerful concentrated OEM customers (Boeing/Airbus/defense primes)
Cyclical end markets: commercial aero build rates, defense budgets and industrial capex all swing
Growth has been substantially bought (Dodge 2021, Specline 2023, VACCO 2025) — acquisition pricing/integration risk and rising capex (true capex $33.2M FY2024 → $73.1M FY2026)
